data.title: Worley Reconfirms FY27 Outlook
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - Worley (WOR.AX) said, for fiscal 2027, it continues to expect mid to high single-digit growth in aggregated revenue and underlying EBITA. Underlying EBITA is expected to be weighted more heavily to the second half than historical norms. The Group noted that first half earnings this financial year will be lower than the prior corresponding period last year.

The company said its approach to capital allocation remains balanced. The Board continues to focus on deploying shareholders' capital where it can generate attractive, risk-adjusted returns.

Worley shares are trading at A$9.76 on Australian Securities Exchange, down 1.31%.

data.title: Microsoft, Intel Expand Azure Infrastructure Partnership Under Long-Term Agreement
data.description:
REDMOND (dpa-AFX) - Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) said it has expanded its long-term partnership with Intel to strengthen Azure infrastructure and support growing demand for cloud and AI computing.

Under the agreement, Microsoft will secure multi-year supplies of Intel Xeon processors, including next-generation server CPUs codenamed Diamond Rapids. The companies will also expand their work on Azure infrastructure and Intel-based hardware systems.

Microsoft said it will become the first company to use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for its custom Azure chips.

The collaboration will also cover Intel Xeon processors with Compute Express Link (CXL), Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) and confidential computing, aimed at improving memory efficiency, database performance and security.

'Our longstanding collaboration with Intel brings together advanced packaging, custom compute, memory and security capabilities to support Azure and drive continued innovation. Together, we are combining silicon and systems engineering to meet growing customer demand for cloud and AI computing,' said Saurabh Dighe, CVP, Azure System & Architecture at Microsoft.

On the Nasdaq, Microsoft shares rose 0.70% in after-hours trading after closing at $508.29 on Wednesday.

data.title: Australia shares drop as miner rout deepens, jobs data fuels slowdown worries
data.description:
Key points:
  • ASX 200 records lowest close since October 15
  • Miners hit near 8-month low
  • Banks end 0.3% lower, paring some earlier losses
  • Soft jobs print lowers rate hike risk, fuels downturn worries

By Shruti Agarwal

Australian shares logged their lowest closing level in over a month on Thursday, as the rout in miners deepened, while weak jobs data that largely removed the risk of rate hikes fed concerns about an economic downturn.

The S&P/ASX 200 index ended 1% lower at 8,730.40 points, its lowest closing level since October 15. The benchmark is down 3.9% so far this week. All but two sectors ended in the red.

Miners hit a near eight-month low, dropping 4%, with heavyweights BHP and Rio Tinto shedding 4.1% and 3.7%, respectively.

In the previous session, copper had its biggest one-day drop since the April 2025 US tariff selloff due to inflation fears, though it has since recovered slightly.

The gold producers' sub-index fell 5.6% to a more than three-month low.

The materials sector has lost roughly 7% this week as rotation out of the sector intensified.

Data showed employment in the country fell for a second straight month in October, while the jobless rate rose to a fresh five-year high, easing concerns about a tight labour market.

The soft print nearly wiped out bets on further rate hikes, and markets are now pricing in a 2.4% chance of a cut at the central bank's December meeting, up from none before the data.

While the data removes rate risk, it also signals slower household spending and weaker earnings growth into 2027, said William Taylor, chief operating officer at ETF Shares.

"That's why we're not seeing the relief rally you might expect," he said.

RBA board members, who voted against a hike this month, had flagged the risk of the economy facing a sharper-than-expected downturn, worries reinforced by mounting evidence of broader layoffs and persistently weak productivity growth.

Financials pared some losses after the data but still ended 0.3% lower.

The rate outlook eases concerns about mortgage stress and bad debts, but a continued rise in unemployment could shift the focus to credit quality, a tougher backdrop for the sector, Taylor said.

New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index slipped 0.1% to 14,247.25 points.

data.title: South African rand slides to year low ahead of rate decision
data.description:
The South African rand weakened to its lowest level of the year against the dollar on Thursday, pressured by a firmer greenback, softer precious-metal prices and uncertainty around local government coalition talks, as investors awaited the central bank's policy decision later in the day.

  • At 0402 GMT, the rand traded at 17.3450 against the dollar , 0.3% weaker than its previous close and near the year's low of 17.36 touched in Asian trade

  • The risk-sensitive rand has come under pressure in recent months amid broader risk aversion, while coalition talks following local government elections have raised questions about the stability of South Africa's Government of National Unity as the African National Congress and Democratic Alliance work to finalise local power-sharing agreements

  • "The local elections are also causing a massive headache, as has the move in commodities," said Adam Phillips of Umkhulu Treasury

  • The dollar hovered near a 19-month high after minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting and hawkish comments from a Fed official reinforced expectations of further interest-rate hikes, weighing on precious metals and leaving South Africa's key export, gold, near a 14-month low

  • Focus later in the session will turn to the South African Reserve Bank's interest-rate decision due around 1300 GMT, where it is widely expected to leave rates unchanged after raising them at its previous meeting

  • South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) was steady in early deals, with the yield at 8.71%

data.title: Blackstone’s plan to acquire 16% stake in IIFL Finance to boost Tier 1 capital ratio
data.description:
Blackstone Inc.’s plan to acquire 16 per cent of IIFL Finance Ltd will strengthen the Indian non-banking financial institution’s (NBFI) regulatory Tier 1 ratio and support its growth, Fitch Ratings said.

The agency observed that the proposed transaction has no immediate effect on IIFL’s ratings (BB-/Stable). Further, the business and franchise benefits, and the implications for IIFL’s risk appetite, will only become clear over time.

The purchase will inject fresh capital and provide Blackstone the right to appoint its representatives to the board. IIFL’s co-founders will contribute equity to avoid dilution of their shareholdings, and the controlling shareholder group will remain unchanged.

“We believe the refreshed shareholder and board composition could alter IIFL’s business strategy, risk appetite and growth trajectory, even if the significant injection of capital and foreign investment supports Indian financial institutions’ capital and funding flexibility,” Fitch Ratings said.

Tier 1 capital ratio to more than double

The fresh equity of ₹6,400 crore (USD 686 million) will broaden IIFL’s capital base, with the pro forma standalone Tier 1 capital ratio more than doubling to 25.7 per cent, from 12.5 per cent at end-September 2026. This follows a recent regulatory reclassification of IIFL’s standalone business as a gold-loan NBFI, which raised its minimum Tier 1 capital requirement from 10 per cent to 12 per cent.

The agency said the equity will provide capital for growth and investment in technology and process improvement, while allowing IIFL to reduce its reliance on wholesale or off-balance-sheet funding amid near-term interest rate volatility.

Focus on secured lending and gold loans

”Our base case is that there will be no large shift in IIFL’s business model, which focuses on secured loans. IIFL has emphasised its intention to boost growth in core product segments, particularly gold-backed lending, through branch expansion and intensification of assets handled per branch and per employee. This should support the earnings profile, provided it maintains adequate underwriting, risk management and cost control,” it said.

Fitch flags risks from aggressive lending

Fitch Ratings cautioned that a material rise in risk appetite, including excessive growth or looser underwriting, could increase the prospects of asset quality deterioration and higher credit costs, and may exert downward pressure on IIFL’s rating. Pressure could also arise if the company renews its appetite for construction financing or unsecured loans, which Fitch generally considers higher risk.

Funding costs expected to ease gradually

The agency noted that the NBFI’s management expects funding costs to ease after the transaction, including through the repayment of existing higher-cost debt, which should support the net interest margin.

“That said, we believe any reduction in funding costs will be gradual. Meanwhile, lower leverage could improve the company’s ability to negotiate borrowing terms with banks and debt investors,” the agency said.

Transaction completion targeted by January 2027

The transaction is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval, and management targets completion by January 2027. The injection will come through a mix of compulsory convertible preference shares and warrants, both of which will be converted into equity within 18 months.

Fitch Ratings said the warrants carry a risk of non-subscription, but they are issued to the co-founders, and we expect them to be fully subscribed. It noted that Blackstone would effectively become IIFL’s main private-equity shareholder.

data.title: Quality Keeps Morgan Stanley Neutral on Treasurys — Market Talk
data.description: Quality is the reason why Morgan Stanley remains neutral on U.S. Treasurys, despite the fact that it is maximum overweight in global equities, its analysts say in a note. "In fact, we keep some exposure to duration because we are max overweight in stocks," they say.As much as there has been a lot of concern that stock-bond return correlations are now stuck in a positive regime and Treasurys have lost their shine as a buffer in the portfolio, "we think this concern is overdone." Bonds have acted as a ballast against the most recent tech sell-off, served their purpose during the cross-asset deleveraging event in February this year, they say, adding that U.S. Treasurys remain a good portfolio diversifier. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
